text: When you work with APIs, you are essentially asking another program for data over the internet. This is done using HTTP requests, such as GET to retrieve information or POST to send new data. Most modern APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and computers to read. Before making requests, you usually need authentication, often in the form of an API key, to prove who you are. However, you must also respect rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a given time. Finally, good error handling is crucial, because network problems or invalid inputs can happen at any moment. Learning to check response codes and handle exceptions will save you hours of debugging later.
